sections.h2: Where to start with a fast Delray Beach sale
sections.html:
Delray Beach is a Palm Beach County city, so your tax bill, deed recording and tax-certificate rules come from county offices. A quick sale usually hinges on three things: how the house looks and works, any mortgage payoff, and the property tax calendar.

The city's own history page describes a place that grew from a small farming village to a city of nearly 70,000 residents, with a historic downtown on Atlantic Avenue and older neighborhoods around it. Older homes near downtown can carry deferred maintenance, while newer ones elsewhere in the city tend to need less. Buyers who use mortgages may ask for repairs. Cash buyers often take the house as-is.

  • List with an agent if you can wait for showings and a lender's timeline.
  • Sell as-is for cash if repairs, a move date or a tax deadline is pressing.
  • Sell to a renovator if the house needs work a mortgage buyer would reject.

The town began as Linton, became Delray in 1898 after crop freezes and a land payment default, and turned into Delray Beach when two municipalities merged on May 11, 1927. The area west of the canal was incorporated in 1911 and the area east of the Intracoastal in 1923.

That split between mainland and barrier island is why Delray still has two distinct feels, a beachside area east of the waterway and inland neighborhoods to the west. The first bridge over the canal went up in 1911. Neighborhood ages differ widely, so ask the title company to search for old easements and unreleased liens on an older parcel, because a long chain of ownership can hide a mortgage that was never formally satisfied.

Old School Square and Atlantic Avenue anchor the downtown, and houses within walking distance often draw buyers who want that setting. The 1913 school building now houses the Cornell Museum of Art and History, and the 1925 high school building is the Crest Theatre.

If your home is in or near a historic area, ask the city's planning staff about any rules for exterior changes before a buyer commits to a renovation plan. A renovation buyer will want to know that early.

The county tax collector mails more than 600,000 property tax bills by November 1, and they are payable from November 1 through March 31. Delinquency starts April 1, and penalties and interest follow. The property appraiser mails the Notice of Proposed Taxes each August.

  • Florida law moves a weekend or holiday deadline to the next working day.
  • Delinquent tax cannot be paid online, and a postmark is not proof of payment once the tax is delinquent.
  • If you sold the house and the bill still came to you, the tax collector has a Property Sold Form so the bill can be redirected.

The county's property tax page also lists an installment plan and a homestead tax deferral. Ask the office whether you qualify before you list.

Under section 201.02 the deed tax is 70 cents on every $100 of consideration, and every party on the deed is liable whichever one agrees to pay. Palm Beach County is not Miami-Dade, so the ordinary statewide rate applies.

The clerk may bill $5.00 on page one and $4.00 per page after it under section 28.24, with trust fund and technology charges on top. Spousal homestead deeds where the only consideration is a mortgage, and divorce deeds for the marital home, are listed as exempt.

Older owners sometimes use lady bird deeds. A Department of Revenue advisement from October 2020 concluded that one, on the facts presented, was not subject to documentary stamp tax because the life tenants kept full powers. That conclusion is specific to those facts, so ask a title attorney before relying on it.

sections.h2: Listing or quick sale: how to compare
sections.html:
Compare the net amount, the time to close and the risk that a deal falls through. A listing can reach more buyers but adds showings, appraisal and loan conditions. Cash can close on your date and tends to skip repair demands.

  1. Get your mortgage payoff in writing.
  2. Check whether property taxes for the current year are paid.
  3. Ask each buyer who pays stamps, title and recording.
  4. Ask for the closing statement ahead of time.

If a foreclosure is pending, the clerk's sale follows final judgment within 20 to 35 days unless the plaintiff agrees to more time.

sections.h2: Keeping your homestead benefit in a move
sections.html:
Portability allows it. If you set up a new Florida homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, the Save Our Homes difference can reduce the new home's assessed value. File Form DR-501T with Form DR-501 by March 1.

Homestead is lost if the property is rented, stops being your permanent home, or you stop being a Florida resident. Owners 65 or older may be offered an added exemption by local ordinance if household income is within the limit, so ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser whether one applies in Delray Beach.

Once you accept, a title company checks the record, prepares the deed and sets the closing date. Bring photo ID, keys and any garage or gate openers. Read the settlement statement before you sign, and confirm how your proceeds will reach you. Your lender is paid off first, taxes are prorated and the balance goes to you after the deed is recorded.

Keep copies of everything you sign. If you are buying another home, ask the title company for your closing figures in advance so your next lender has what it needs.

faqs.q: When did Delray Beach become a city?
faqs.a: The City of Delray Beach was formed on May 11, 1927, when the Town of Delray Beach and the City of Delray united. They had been incorporated separately, in 1923 and 1911.

faqs.q: What was Delray Beach called before?
faqs.a: It started as Linton, named in 1895 for a congressman in the settlement group. Residents changed it to Delray in 1898 after freezes damaged crops.

faqs.q: When are Palm Beach County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Bills are payable from November 1 through March 31, and delinquent taxes cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: Is there an early payment discount in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Yes: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, with none in March.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Delray Beach?
faqs.a: The contract decides who pays, but all parties are liable. The statewide deed rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.
